title: What to Verify Before Switching Media Platforms
summary: Learn how to vet a media platform migration by testing one real project for metadata, version history, permissions, folder structure, and future export terms.
body_text: The safest way to switch media platforms is to treat the migration like a post workflow, not a file copy. You're moving the working memory of your team: clip names, rights notes, review history, folder logic, access rules, versions, proxies, comments, captions, transcripts, and the small bits of metadata that help a producer find the right shot six months later. A vendor can usually show you a clean demo with a sample folder. The question is whether your real library survives the move in a form your editors, assistants, post supervisors, and production teams can actually use. Migration area Ask the vendor Prove it in the pilot Metadata Will custom fields, embedded metadata, rights notes, captions, transcripts, and technical metadata remain searchable and exportable? Search for known values and confirm they land in usable fields, not a generic notes dump. Version history Will prior versions stay connected to the current asset with comments, approvals, timestamps, and owners intact? Open a real version stack and confirm reviewers can tell which notes and approvals belong to which cut. Permissions How will internal roles, external reviewers, folder access, download rights, expired links, and view-only rules map? Log in as a producer, assistant, client, and reviewer to confirm each user sees only what they should. Folder structure Will the full folder tree, empty template folders, original paths, long names, and duplicate names survive? Compare the migrated project against the source and confirm assistants can still find assets where they expect them. Start with one representative project Don't begin with the whole library, and don't test with a tidy folder someone made for evaluation. Pick one real project that has the normal messiness of your workflow. Use one real project with the normal workflow mess, not a sanitized sample folder. A good test project usually includes: Camera originals or high-res masters Proxies or mezzanine files Multiple cut versions Review comments or approval notes Custom metadata fields Rights or usage restrictions A nested folder structure A mix of file types, including stills, audio, captions, graphics, and project files Internal users, external reviewers, and client access Any platform should be able to upload files. Use the pilot to prove that the relationships between files survive: which proxy belongs to which master , which version replaced which edit, which comments apply to which asset, which folder rules matter, and which people should still have access . Run this pilot early, while you still have negotiating room with the vendor. If the test exposes problems, you want time to change the migration plan, adjust field mapping, or decide that the platform isn't a fit. Metadata is where migrations break Most media teams don't realize how much they rely on metadata until it disappears. Filename and upload date are the obvious fields, but the important fields are usually the ones your team created over time. Ask the vendor how the new platform will import and store each type of metadata , how your team will search it, and how your team can export it later. That includes both embedded file metadata and platform-level metadata. The fields worth testing include: Clip name, reel name, scene, take, camera, shoot date, and timecode Custom tags, labels, campaign names, show names, and episode numbers Rights notes, territory restrictions, expiration dates, and talent usage limits Transcript text, speaker labels, captions, and subtitles Approval status, air status, legal status, or archive status Original path, source platform ID, and any unique asset identifier Technical metadata like codec, resolution, frame rate, audio channel layout, and duration Ask the vendor to show you exactly where the platform stores each field, how users will search it, and how your team can export it again. Metadata should stay attached to the asset in structured, searchable form. For post teams, identifiers matter. Reel names, timecode , and source file names often connect offline edits, proxies, masters, and conform workflows. If the migration flattens, renames, or treats those values as generic tags, the platform may still look organized while becoming less useful for editorial. If your current system has custom fields, ask whether the new platform supports the same field types. A dropdown field, free-text field, multi-select tag, date field, and rights window aren't interchangeable. Migrating everything into a notes field may technically preserve the text, but it can destroy filtering, reporting, and automation. Version history needs more than the latest file A lot of platforms can migrate the current version of a file, but fewer can preserve the version stack in a way that still makes sense to a producer reviewing a spot, trailer, episode, or social cut. Ask how the platform handles existing versions during migration. You want to know whether versions remain connected or become separate standalone files. Test the cases your team actually uses: Rough cut, fine cut, locked cut, textless, final, and revised final Client review versions with comments attached Assets with the same filename uploaded at different times Versions that changed format, such as ProRes to H.264 review file Old versions that should remain viewable but not downloadable Approval states attached to specific versions, not just the asset as a whole Version history often supports accountability. If a client approved V4, but the platform only shows the latest upload, your team loses context. If comments from V3 appear on V5 without clear separation, reviewers get confused. If renamed files break the version stack, assistants may spend days rebuilding history by hand. A usable migration should preserve the relationship between versions, the timestamps, the uploader or owner where possible, and the review context around each version. If the vendor can't preserve all of that, make sure you know what will be lost and whether your team can live with it. Permissions rarely map perfectly Permissions are one of the easiest areas to underestimate. On paper, both platforms may support admins, members, reviewers, folders, links, and external users, but in practice, the permission models may work very differently. Ask the vendor to map your current permission structure into their model before migration, and don't wait until after the files arrive. The mapping should cover: Internal admins, producers, editors, assistants, legal, marketing, and archive users External clients, agencies, vendors, freelancers, and reviewers Folder-level access File-level access Share links and their expiration dates Download permissions Watermarking or view-only restrictions Approval permissions Revoked users and inactive accounts The hard part is preserving intent. If a client could only view a specific folder, they shouldn't suddenly see the whole project. If a freelance editor had upload rights but not admin rights, that distinction should survive. If legal had access to rights-restricted material but marketing didn't, the migration shouldn't flatten those roles into a single “team member” permission. Be especially careful with inherited permissions. Some platforms apply access from a parent folder down through every subfolder. Others allow exceptions at lower levels. If your existing library depends on those exceptions, the migration can accidentally open or block sensitive material. During the test migration, log in as a few real user types, and don't just inspect the admin view. Check what a producer sees, what an assistant sees, what a client sees, and what an external reviewer sees. Check permissions from real user perspectives, not just the admin view. Folder structure is more than cosmetic Folder structure carries operational meaning because it tells assistants where to drop new media, tells editors where to find proxies, tells producers which assets are approved, and tells archive teams how the project was delivered. Ask whether the new platform preserves the full folder tree, including empty folders if your team uses them as templates. Also ask how it handles illegal characters, duplicate folder names, long paths, and naming collisions. A migration can look successful while still damaging the folder logic. Common problems include: Flattened folder trees Renamed folders due to unsupported characters Duplicate folders merged together Empty template folders omitted Files moved into generic “Imported” folders Original paths lost Sort order changed in a way that disrupts assistant workflows For post-production teams, the original path can be useful even after the move because it helps trace where an asset came from, rebuild broken references, and compare the migrated library against the source. If the new platform can't preserve the exact path as structure, ask whether it can preserve it as metadata. This is also where you should test mixed media. A real project folder may include camera media, exports, thumbnails, cue sheets, PDFs, captions, audio stems, graphics, NLE project files, and delivery packages. Make sure the platform accepts the file types you actually store, not just the video files it can preview. Watch for proxy, master, and conform assumptions A media platform migration isn't the same as moving an NLE timeline, but the same lesson applies: interchange formats and migration tools only carry the data their designers built them to carry. If a vendor says “we preserve everything,” ask what “everything” means in technical terms. For editorial and finishing teams, the risky areas are usually relationships and references: Proxy-to-master relationships Source filename consistency Timecode and reel metadata Sidecar files such as captions, LUTs, XMLs, AAFs, EDLs, and CSVs Review files connected to high-res masters Watermarked screeners connected to clean exports Audio stems connected to picture versions If your team ever conforms, relinks, rebuilds timelines, or references old edits, don't let the migration strip away the data that makes that possible. The platform doesn't need to be an NLE, but it shouldn't make your NLE workflows harder. This is another reason to test with a real project, because a sample folder won't reveal whether the migrated library still supports the way your assistants prep, track, and hand off media. Ask how the migration will actually run Once the pilot looks good, ask for the operational plan. A good migration plan should explain how data moves, how long it will take, who owns each task, and how your team and the vendor will validate the result. You want practical answers to questions like: Will the vendor pull from the old platform, receive a drive, or require your team to upload? Can the migration run incrementally, or does it require a hard cutover? Who retries failed files, and how? How does the vendor or platform detect duplicates? What happens to files that the new platform can't preview? How will your team or the vendor use checksums or file counts to confirm completeness ? What reports will you receive after each batch? Can users keep working during migration, or does the library need to freeze? For large media libraries, time estimates need to include more than bandwidth. Upload speed, API limits, throttling, file count, small-file overhead, transcode or proxy generation, metadata import, and human review all affect the schedule. A 200 TB library made of huge camera files behaves differently from a 20 TB library with hundreds of thousands of small assets, thumbnails, sidecars, and exports, and file count can be as painful as file size. Define the cutover in human terms The technical migration may finish before the team is ready to work in the new platform. Plan the cutover around active productions, review cycles, delivery deadlines, and client approvals. For many teams, the cleanest path is a phased move: Migrate and validate one completed project Migrate a small group of active projects Freeze changes in the old platform for a defined window Move the remaining library in batches Keep the old platform read-only for a short overlap period The overlap period matters because it gives assistants and producers time to compare projects, catch missing metadata, and answer the inevitable “where did this go?” questions without blocking active work. Don't let both systems stay editable for too long, though, because that creates split-brain problems where comments, versions, and approvals live in two places. If you need an overlap, make the rules clear: one system is the source of truth, the other is reference-only. Know what happens if you leave later A platform switch is also the moment to ask about your next exit. That may feel premature, but it's much easier to negotiate and understand export terms before you sign than when you're already trying to leave. Ask what your data looks like on export, including the structure and context around the media files. Exit terms should produce an organized export, not loose disconnected files. The exit discussion should cover: Original media export Proxy and preview file export Folder structure export Metadata export format Version history export Comment and approval history export User and permission export Rights data export Captions, transcripts, and sidecar files Audit logs or activity history Costs for bulk export, storage retrieval, or support Timeline for account access after cancellation If the answer is “you can download your files,” keep asking, because that may be fine for a simple storage bucket, but it isn't enough for a production media library. Your team needs to understand whether your team can use the exported data in another system or whether it becomes a pile of files plus a few CSVs that only make sense after weeks of cleanup. Also ask whether the platform keeps any proprietary-only data. AI tags, transcripts, review annotations, approval states, and custom fields may be useful inside the system but difficult to move out. That doesn't automatically make the platform a bad choice, but you should know which parts of your workflow become platform-dependent. The practical decision A media platform is ready for your library when it can prove four things with your real project: metadata shows up in usable fields, version history remains intelligible, permissions preserve intent, and folder structure comes out intact. If any of those fail, the cost includes migration cleanup, slower editorial prep, weaker search, confused approvals, rights risk, and more manual reconstruction by the people who are already carrying too much of the workflow. The best vendor conversations are specific. Bring one messy project. Ask them to migrate it. Open it as different users. Search for known metadata. Compare the version stack. Check the folder tree. Export the result. Then decide based on what survived. FAQ Run a pilot migration with one real project that reflects your normal workflow. Use a project with versions, comments, custom metadata, rights notes, nested folders, mixed file types, and real user permissions. A clean sample folder won't reveal whether the new platform can preserve the relationships your team depends on. Aspect provides complimentary migration from any cloud or local platform and preserves metadata, folder structure, rights, and version history. It depends on how the vendor maps it. Basic fields like filename and upload date are usually simple, but custom fields, rights data, transcripts, timecode, reel names, approval states, and technical metadata need to be tested. Ask where each field will land, whether it remains searchable, and how it can be exported later. Version history preserves the context behind approvals, comments, revisions, and delivery decisions. If only the latest file migrates, producers and reviewers may lose the record of what changed, who approved which cut, and which comments applied to each version. Not always. Platforms often use different permission models, even if they use similar labels such as admin, member, reviewer, or client. The important goal is to preserve intent, such as who can view, download, upload, approve, or access specific folders. Test permissions by logging in as different user types, not only as an admin. Ask how your media, metadata, folder structure, version history, comments, permissions, rights data, captions, transcripts, and audit history can be exported. Also ask about bulk export costs, support fees, proprietary data, and how long you retain account access after cancellation. Run a pilot on one real project that includes versions, permissions, metadata, folders, review notes, rights fields, and mixed media types. Aspect supports migration from cloud or local platforms and preserves metadata, folder structure, rights, and version history as part of its supported migration.

title: Enova’s 2026 Partnership with Junior Achievement of Chicago: Investing in the Next Generation
summary: Financial literacy is not a given for everyone. It is taught, practiced and reinforced. For many students in Chicago, the classroom is the only place those lessons happen. For the second year, Enova has partnered with Junior Achievement (JA) of Chicago to widen that access.
body_text: Enova’s 2026 Partnership with Junior Achievement of Chicago: Investing in the Next Generation August 19, 2026 Financial literacy is not a given for everyone. It is taught, practiced and reinforced. For many students in Chicago, the classroom is the only place those lessons happen. For the second year, Enova has partnered with Junior Achievement (JA) of Chicago to widen that access. The 2026 partnership supported 37 education partners across Chicago, including elementary schools, high schools and community organizations. Together, these partners delivered 123 classes reaching over 2,400 students. Junior Achievement works with a wide range of school communities, where the share of students from low-to-moderate-income households runs from under 15% to 95%. What makes the model work is its ability to adapt. Elementary students at Ashburn Community Elementary School completed “JA Our City” and “JA Ourselves.” Chicago Park District sites ran “JA More Than Money” across 12 classes. At Robert J. Richardson Middle School, where 88% of families qualify as low-to-moderate-income, eight classes of students worked through “JA Economics for Success.” High schoolers at Perspectives Charter School participated in “JA Town” across eight classes. A kindergartener and a high school senior encounter different lessons, but each leaves with skills matched to where they are in life. That range matters because the gap Junior Achievement works to close is not evenly distributed. According to the 2026 State of Financial Education Report from Next Gen Personal Finance (NGPF), 35% of public high school students in the class of 2026 were required to take a standalone personal finance course. This figure shrinks to 15% in schools where more than 75% of students qualify for free or reduced-price lunch. The students least likely to receive financial literacy lessons at school are often the same students with the fewest resources at home to fill the gap. Junior Achievement closes that gap through application, not just lectures. Students build mock businesses, manage simulated portfolios and make important decisions inside an environment built for learning. Enova employees have seen this firsthand. Last year, team members supported JA Town, working alongside students as they navigated budgeting and salary challenges. Employees have a running list of volunteer opportunities, from in-person JA lessons to virtual career day presentations that give students visibility into careers across finance and tech. The gap is close to home. In Illinois, where Enova is headquartered, NGPF found that only 24% of public high school students have a local requirement to take a standalone, one-semester personal finance course before graduating. That requirement comes from individual districts rather than the state, which means access depends largely on where a student happens to enroll. For the roughly 75% of Illinois students without that requirement, programs like Junior Achievement’s are often the only structured financial education they will receive. ❮ Enova Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results

title: Scheduled callbacks for Giga voice agents
summary: Giga’s voice AI agents can now schedule and place callbacks on their own. A customer who gets interrupted mid-call picks a time, and the agent calls back then — carrying the conversation’s context and memory forward, so nobody has to repeat themselves.
body_text: Customers are much more likely to convert when you reach them at an optimal time. That’s why with Giga, customers can now request a callback. Giga’s voice AI agents can now schedule and place callbacks on their own—keeping a conversation’s context and memory in place until your customer is ready to chat. Customers never have to repeat their requests or rehash the conversation. Before today, when customers got interrupted mid-call, it was the end of the conversation. You might document it in their ticket, but in all likelihood, you’ll miss that callback window. It may be after business hours, or perhaps you’re just in a long customer queue, so you need to call back.

title: Identity Verification Software in 2026: A Buyer's Guide
summary: What identity verification software does, what it really costs in 2026, and how to compare Didit, iDenfy, Sumsub, and Veriff on price, coverage, and fraud.
body_text: Back to blog Blog · August 17, 2026 Identity Verification Software in 2026: A Buyer's Guide What identity verification software does, how the 2026 fraud landscape changes the requirements, and how to compare providers on real per-verification cost, coverage, speed, and compliance, with a pricing table built from public pricing pages. By Didit · August 17, 2026 · Updated Aug 17, 2026 Identity verification software confirms that the person opening an account is real, present, and who they claim to be. It reads a government-issued ID, matches the holder's face to the document with a liveness check, and screens the result against sanctions and fraud databases, then returns an automated decision. In 2026, choosing a provider comes down to four questions: what the software actually checks, what it costs per verification once add-ons are included, how much of the world it covers, and whether its fraud detection keeps up with AI-generated attacks. This guide answers all four. Key Takeaways Identity verification software combines document checks, biometrics, and database screening into one automated decision, delivered through an API, SDK, or no-code workflow. The fraud problem is growing on both ends: US consumers reported $12.5 billion lost to fraud in 2024 , a 25% jump over the prior year, while sophisticated fraud attempts rose 180% as attackers adopted AI tooling. Deepfakes are now a mainstream attack vector: they account for 1 in 5 biometric fraud attempts , and injection attacks that bypass the camera entirely grew 40% year over year. Add-ons decide the real price. Published base rates run from $0.33 to $1.85 per verification, but liveness, AML screening, and proof of address are often billed separately and can double the cost per user. Monthly minimums decide who can start. Most providers require $49–$299 per month before the first verification; Didit has no minimum and includes 500 free verifications every month. What Is Identity Verification Software? Identity verification software is a system that confirms a real person is behind an account or transaction. It authenticates a government-issued ID document, matches the holder's face to that document using biometric comparison and a liveness test, and screens the verified identity against sanctions lists, politically exposed persons (PEP) databases, and fraud signals. Delivered through an API, SDK, or hosted flow, it returns an automated approve, decline, or review decision and produces an audit trail regulators can inspect. The category goes by several names. Compliance teams say KYC (Know Your Customer) software, product teams say IDV (identity verification), and regulators talk about customer due diligence. The underlying capability is the same, and the buyers are too: fintechs and neobanks onboarding account holders, crypto exchanges meeting MiCA and Travel Rule obligations, marketplaces verifying sellers before payouts, mobility platforms validating driver's licenses, and iGaming operators running mandatory age checks. What the Software Actually Checks A useful way to map the category is the lifecycle of a user: authenticate, verify, monitor. Most vendors sell pieces of it; the evaluation question is how many pieces you need and whether they run on one platform or three. Document verification. OCR and forensic analysis of passports, national IDs, and driver's licenses: fonts, holograms, MRZ checksums, signs of reprinting or digital tampering. Coverage is measured in countries and document types supported. Biometric verification. A selfie is matched 1:1 against the document photo. A liveness check (passive, with no user instructions, or active) confirms a live human is in front of the camera rather than a photo, replay, or deepfake. Database and registry validation. The extracted identity is checked against authoritative sources: government registries, telco records, credit bureaus. AML screening. Names are screened against sanctions lists, PEP databases, and adverse media, with fuzzy matching for transliterations. Regulated businesses also need ongoing re-screening, not just a check at signup. Fraud signal analysis. IP and device intelligence, duplicate-face detection across accounts, blocklists, and injection-attack detection that catches manipulated video fed directly into the verification API. Orchestration and case management. Workflow rules that route users by risk tier or country, plus a console where analysts review edge cases and document decisions for audits. Why the Bar Is Higher in 2026 Two datasets frame the problem. On the victim side, the US Federal Trade Commission logged more than 1.1 million identity theft reports in 2024, and consumers reported $12.5 billion in fraud losses, up 25% in a single year . On the attacker side, Sumsub's 2025 identity fraud research puts the global identity fraud rate at 2.2% of verification attempts, and records a 180% increase in sophisticated fraud compared with 2024 as simple tactics stopped working and attackers shifted to AI-generated identities and coordinated account abuse. The nature of the attacks has changed more than the volume. Entrust's identity fraud report , built on more than 1 billion verification events across 195 countries, found that deepfakes now account for one in five biometric fraud attempts, deepfaked selfie attempts grew 58% in a year, and injection attacks, where fraudsters bypass the camera and feed synthetic video straight into the verification pipeline, surged 40% year over year. The practical consequence for buyers: a provider whose anti-spoofing stops at "blink twice" screens out honest users while letting tooled-up fraud through. Ask vendors specifically about deepfake detection, injection-attack detection, and how fast their models are updated when a new attack pattern appears. How to Compare Providers: Six Criteria Real per-verification cost. Take the advertised base rate, then add every module you actually need: liveness, AML screening, proof of address, manual review. Add-on pricing changes the rankings, as the table below shows. Commercial terms. Check the monthly minimum, whether an annual commitment is required, and whether you can test at production volume before signing anything. A free tier or pay-as-you-go plan removes procurement as a blocker. Coverage. Countries, document types, and languages supported, plus direct government database connections in the markets you operate in. This is the hardest capability to retrofit. Speed and completion. Verification sits inside your signup funnel, so measure it there: compare median decision time and flow completion rates on low-end devices and slow networks during a pilot, not just under demo conditions. Fraud detection depth. Number and type of fraud signals, in-house versus resold detection models, duplicate-face search, and documented handling of deepfakes and injection attacks. Compliance and integration. SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 certifications, GDPR posture (including whether biometric data is stored at all), audit trails, and developer experience: public docs, instant sandbox, SDKs, webhooks, and migration paths. What Identity Verification Software Costs in 2026 All figures below come from the providers' public pricing pages, checked in August 2026. Custom-quote enterprise vendors (Jumio, Onfido/Entrust, Trulioo) are excluded because they publish no comparable numbers. Didit iDenfy Sumsub Veriff Core verification price $0.33 (Full KYC bundle: ID + liveness + face match + IP/device) $1.35 per verification $1.35 (entry plan); $1.85 (higher tier) $0.80 (Essential); $1.39 (Plus) Monthly minimum $0 $135 $149–$299 $49–$99 Free tier 500 verifications/month, ongoing Not listed on pricing page Not listed on pricing page Not listed on pricing page Sanctions/PEP screening +$0.20 (1,300+ lists) +$0.50 add-on Varies by plan +$0.64 add-on Proof of address +$0.20 +$1.00 add-on Varies by plan Not listed Liveness Included in bundle 3D face liveness +$0.25 add-on Included Included Those add-ons change the totals quickly. A verification flow with liveness, sanctions screening, and proof of address prices out at $0.73 on Didit ($0.33 + $0.20 + $0.20), while the same flow reaches $3.10 on iDenfy ($1.35 + $0.25 + $0.50 + $1.00) before its $135 monthly minimum. Veriff's Essential plan starts lower at $0.80, but adding its PEP and sanctions check brings a compliance-grade flow to $1.44 per user. The numbers are all public; few buyers run the full-flow calculation before signing. Minimums matter for a different reason: they set the floor for testing. A $135–$299 monthly commitment is trivial for a bank and meaningful for a seed-stage startup verifying 300 users a month. This is why per-check pricing with no minimum has become the entry point for most new implementations. Where Didit Fits Didit is infrastructure for identity and fraud: one API covering both halves of the problem, identity (KYC, KYB) and fraud (transaction monitoring, wallet screening, AML), across the full lifecycle from authentication to verification to continuous monitoring. The relevant facts for an evaluation, all from the public pricing page : Full KYC costs $0.33 per verification (ID verification + passive liveness + face match + IP and device analysis), with per-module pricing published for 25+ modules: ID verification $0.15, passive liveness $0.10, AML screening $0.20 across 1,300+ sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media lists, proof of address $0.20. 500 verifications are free every month, with no credit card, no minimums, and no annual contract. Coverage spans 220+ countries and 14,000+ document types, with government database validation where registries allow it. Didit is ISO/IEC 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certified and a participant in an EU financial sandbox program. Integration is developer-first: public docs, an instant sandbox, SDKs for web and mobile, a no-code workflow builder, and an MCP server so AI agents can trigger verifications directly. Whether Didit is the right choice depends on your requirements; the evaluation criteria above apply to us as much as to anyone. The free tier exists so you can run that evaluation on production traffic instead of a slide deck. Ready to Compare for Yourself? The most reliable way to choose is to test. Build your exact flow in two or three sandboxes, send real traffic through each, and compare completion rates, decision quality, and the full-flow price per verified user. Create a free Didit account (500 verifications per month are included, forever) or read the docs to see the API before you sign up. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What is the difference between identity verification software and KYC software? In practice they describe the same category from different angles. KYC (Know Your Customer) is the regulatory obligation: confirming customer identity and screening for financial-crime risk under AML rules. Identity verification software is the technology that fulfills it through document checks, biometrics, and database screening. Vendors in this market typically serve both the regulated use case (KYC/AML) and non-regulated ones like marketplace trust or age gating. How much does identity verification software cost? Published base rates in 2026 range from $0.33 to $1.85 per verification among providers with public pricing, before add-ons such as AML screening ($0.20–$0.64) or proof of address ($0.20–$1.00). Most providers also require monthly minimums between $49 and $299; Didit charges no minimum and includes 500 free verifications per month. Enterprise vendors without public pricing quote custom annual contracts. How fast should identity verification be? Vendor speed claims are hard to compare on paper, so measure speed in a pilot instead. What matters is the whole flow on your users' actual devices: document capture, selfie, decision, and any retries. Run the same test traffic through each provider and compare median end-to-end time and completion rates, especially on older phones and weak connections, where flows differ most. Can identity verification software detect deepfakes? Some can, and this is where providers differ most. Deepfakes now account for 1 in 5 biometric fraud attempts , and injection attacks that skip the camera entirely grew 40% in a year. Ask providers whether their liveness detection is certified against presentation attacks, whether they detect injection attacks specifically, and how quickly their models are retrained when new attack tooling appears. Do I need ongoing monitoring or just a check at signup? Regulated businesses generally need both. A signup check confirms who the customer is on day one, but sanctions and PEP status can change after onboarding, which is why providers sell ongoing monitoring as a distinct module: Veriff lists it at +$0.09 per check , and Didit's ongoing AML re-screens every user continuously against 1,300+ lists . If you fall under AML rules, price ongoing monitoring into the comparison from the start rather than bolting it on later.

title: Globalstar Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Generated second quarter 2026 revenue of $64.8 million with record high Commercial IoT subscriber activations. Continued progress on regulatory approval process in connection with the previously announced Merger Agreement with Amazon, with expiration of the waiting period under the HSR Act in July
body_text: Globalstar Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results August 6, 2026 at 8:00 AM EDT Generated second quarter 2026 revenue of $64.8 million with record high Commercial IoT subscriber activations. Continued progress on regulatory approval process in connection with the previously announced Merger Agreement with Amazon, with expiration of the waiting period under the HSR Act in July 2026. Continued execution of next-generation satellite constellation initiatives with launch of first set of replacement satellites rescheduled for later this month and further development of third-generation satellites . COVINGTON, La., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Globalstar, Inc. (Nasdaq: GSAT) (“Globalstar” or the “Company”), a next-generation telecommunications infrastructure and technology provider, today announced its financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Capitalized terms not defined herein have the meaning given to such terms in our periodic reports. "During the second quarter, we remained focused on disciplined execution across our business while continuing to invest in the technologies and infrastructure that support our long-term strategy," said Dr. Paul E. Jacobs, Chief Executive Officer of Globalstar. "We continue to make meaningful progress across our product, network and commercial initiatives while advancing the regulatory process associated with our previously announced Merger Agreement with Amazon. I am proud of our team's continued execution and commitment to delivering innovative connectivity solutions for our customers." RECENT OPERATIONAL HIGHLIGHTS Transaction Update : The proposed transaction with Amazon is progressing through the regulatory approval process with the HSR waiting period having expired on July 17, 2026. Globalstar and Amazon are actively engaged with remaining regulatory authorities, including the FCC and certain international merger control, foreign investment and satellite and communications authorities. The transaction is expected to close in 2027 and remains subject to the satisfaction of remaining closing conditions including, among others, receipt of outstanding regulatory approvals and Globalstar's achievement of certain HIBLEO-4 replacement satellite milestones. C ontinued Execution of Satellite Network Initiatives: Globalstar continued execution of its next-generation satellite replacement and expansion initiatives, including preparation for the launch of its first set of replacement satellites, which will support Globalstar’s current-generation LEO constellation, and further development of its third-generation satellites and ground infrastructure. Globalstar is expanding its international network of ground stations in order to support its third-generation C-3 satellite system with active construction projects in multiple countries across North and South America as well as Europe and Asia. These initiatives represent important components of the Company's long-term strategy pursuant to the Updated Services Agreements to enhance network resilience, capacity and service capabilities. Commercial Momentum Across Connectivity Solutions: Globalstar continued to see commercial engagement across its satellite and terrestrial connectivity portfolio, including customer interest in its RM200M satellite communications module and ongoing demand for mission-critical connectivity solutions. The Company also continued expanding opportunities within government and defense markets while supporting customers across its terrestrial and satellite offerings. SECOND QUARTER FINANCIAL REVIEW Revenue Total revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $64.8 million, including $60.0 million of service revenue and $4.8 million of revenue generated from subscriber equipment sales. Service revenue decreased $3.2 million, or 5%, during the second quarter of 2026 compared to the prior year's second quarter, primarily due to a decrease in wholesale capacity service revenue resulting from the timing of service fees associated with the reimbursement of network-related costs. The second quarter of 2025 included out of period wholesale capacity services revenue of $6.6 million; excluding this item, service revenue during the second quarter of 2026 would have increased $3.4 million compared to the prior period. Declines in Duplex and SPOT service revenue due to subscriber churn over the last twelve months also contributed to the decrease in service revenue. Partially offsetting these decreases was an increase in Commercial IoT service revenue due to growth in the subscriber base during the second quarter of 2026; we achieved record high Commercial IoT subscriber activations during the second quarter of 2026, contributing to an over 20% increase in gross activations on a last twelve-month basis. Revenue from subscriber equipment sales increased $0.8 million, or 21%, compared to the prior year's second quarter primarily due to a higher volume of Commercial IoT device sales, and to a lesser extent, but meaningful from a strategic growth perspective, the sale of XCOM RAN systems. (Loss) Income from Operations Loss from operations was $4.8 million during the second quarter of 2026, compared to income from operations of $6.1 million during the prior year's second quarter. Higher operating expenses and a decrease in service revenue (discussed above) contributed to this change. The increase in operating expenses was due primarily to higher marketing, general and administrative (“MG&A”) expenses and cost of services offset partially by lower stock-based compensation and depreciation expense. MG&A expenses were higher than the prior year's second quarter due primarily to increased legal and other professional fees related to the Amazon transaction. Consistent with previous quarters, higher cost of services resulted primarily from network operating costs to support the build out of our next-generation ground network infrastructure, a significant portion of which are reimbursed to us and recognized as revenue. Costs to support XCOM technology development also increased during the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Also contributing to the increase in cost of services and MG&A expenses was the recognition of employee retention credits received in the second quarter of 2025 that did not recur in 2026. Net (Loss) Income Net loss was $26.5 million for the second quarter of 2026, compared to net income of $19.2 million for the prior year's second quarter. Net loss was impacted by unfavorable changes in foreign currency losses and gains due to the remeasurement of intercompany balances as well as higher interest expense resulting from our recognition of non-cash imputed interest related to the 2024 Prepayment Agreement. Unfavorable changes in (loss) income from operations (discussed above) also impacted the net loss during the quarter. Offsetting these items was a noncash gain on the contingent interest feature within the 2024 Debt Repayment resulting from the achievement of certain milestones under our agreements with the Customer pursuant to the Updated Services Agreements. As a result of the adoption of ASU 2025-07, we are no longer required to bifurcate the embedded derivative associated with the 2024 Debt Repayment; accordingly the quarterly noncash mark-to-market adjustments ceased in 2026. Adjusted EBITDA Adjusted EBITDA was $26.0 million during the second quarter of 2026 compared to $35.8 million during the prior year's second quarter. This decrease was due to higher operating expenses (excluding adjustments for non-cash or non-recurring items) and lower revenue, primarily driven by the out of period service revenue recognized in the second quarter of 2025, as discussed above. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure. For more information, refer to “Reconciliation of GAAP Net Income (Loss) to Non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA.” YEAR TO DATE FINANCIAL REVIEW Revenue Total revenue for the first six months of 2026 was $134.8 million, including $126.7 million of service revenue and $8.1 million of revenue generated from subscriber equipment sales, compared to $127.2 million for the first six months of 2025. Service revenue increased $6.4 million, or 5%, during the first six months of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025 primarily due to higher wholesale capacity services resulting from additional service fees associated with the reimbursement of network-related costs. Consistent with the quarterly results previously discussed, higher Commercial IoT subscribers increased service revenue for the first six months of 2026 partially offset by lower service revenue due to fewer Duplex and SPOT subscribers. Also increasing service revenue for the period was higher revenue associated with our service agreement with Parsons Corporation as we moved beyond the proof of concept phase and into the first year of service. Revenue from subscriber equipment sales increased $1.2 million, or 18%, for the first six months of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025 consistent with the quarterly discussion above. Income (Loss) from Operations Income from operations was $3.4 million during the first six months of 2026, compared to loss from operations of $2.4 million during the same period in 2025. During the first six months of 2026, higher revenue was partially offset by higher operating expenses, as discussed above. Consistent with the quarterly discussion above, operating expenses were higher due primarily to higher MG&A expenses and cost of services offset by lower stock-based compensation and depreciation expense. Also contributing to the increase in cost of services and MG&A expenses was the recognition of employee retention credits received in both the first and second quarters of 2025 that did not recur in 2026. The fluctuation in operating expenses was favorably impacted by a noncash disposal of assets recognized during the first quarter of 2025 that did not recur in 2026. Net (Loss) Income Net loss was $41.4 million for the first six months of 2026, compared to net income of $1.9 million during the same period in 2025. The variances driving net loss and income are consistent with the quarterly discussion above. Adjusted EBITDA Adjusted EBITDA was $59.4 million during the first six months of 2026 compared to $66.1 million during the same period in 2025. Higher revenue was more than offset by higher operating expenses (excluding adjustments for non-cash or non-recurring items). Specifically, while we continue to enhance and develop our XCOM RAN product and service offerings, we have incurred costs, primarily for personnel, in advance of significant revenue. Also, as previously described, 2025 Adjusted EBITDA benefited from out of period service revenue of $6.6 million that was recognized in the second quarter of 2025. Liquidity As of June 30, 2026, we held cash and cash equivalents of $409.8 million, compared to $447.5 million as of December 31, 2025. During the first six months of 2026, net cash flows generated from operations were approximately $159.7 million, capital expenditures were $208.3 million and net cash flows from financing activities were $10.6 million. Cash and cash equivalents were also positively impacted by a $0.3 million effect of exchange rate changes. Operating cash flows during the first six months of 2026 included $104.8 million received in connection with the Infrastructure Prepayment, $15.0 million in accelerated service fee payment from the Customer pursuant to the Updated Services Agreements as well as other cash flows generated from the business. Capital expenditures were primarily associated with our commitments under the Updated Services Agreements related to the deployment of the replacement satellites and Extended MSS Network. Financing activities for the first six months of 2026 reflected a draw pursuant to the 2023 Funding Agreement, offset by the final recoupment under the 2021 Funding Agreement as well as preferred stock dividend payments. Adjusted free cash flow during the first six months of 2026 was $43.5 million compared to $77.9 million during the same period in 2025. This decrease was primarily due to the timing of cash receipts pursuant to the Updated Services Agreements, specifically $15.0 million in accelerated service fees paid to us during the first six months of 2026 compared to $30.0 million during the first six months of 2025 as well as the timing of service fees associated with the reimbursement of network-related costs (as discussed above). Adjusted free cash flow is a non-GAAP financial measure. For more information, refer to “Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Adjusted Free Cash Flow.” The principal amount of our debt was $423.7 million at June 30, 2026, compared to $410.0 million at December 31, 2025. This increase was due to the issuance of debt under the 2023 Funding Agreement totaling $19.9 million during 2026 offset by the final recoupment of $6.3 million under the 2021 Funding Agreement. PMB Politeknik Negeri Jakarta 2026: Jalur Masuk, Prodi, Biaya, dan Cara Daftar
summary: Simak informasi PMB PNJ 2026, mulai dari jalur SNBP, SNBT, Ujian Mandiri, dan Mandiri Prestasi, pilihan program studi, biaya pendaftaran, UKT, jadwal, hingga cara daftar.
body_text: Daftar isi PMB Politeknik Negeri Jakarta 2026 Jadwal, Jalur Masuk, Program Studi, Biaya Kuliah, dan Cara Daftar Politeknik Negeri Jakarta (PNJ) merupakan perguruan tinggi negeri berbasis vokasi yang berlokasi di Depok. PNJ menawarkan berbagai program studi di bidang teknik, teknologi, bisnis, akuntansi, administrasi, hingga grafika dan penerbitan, dengan pilihan jenjang Diploma dan Sarjana Terapan. Bagi calon mahasiswa yang ingin kuliah di PNJ, informasi mengenai jalur masuk, pilihan program studi, biaya pendaftaran, UKT, hingga jadwal seleksi perlu diketahui sebelum melakukan pendaftaran. Profil Politeknik Negeri Jakarta Politeknik Negeri Jakarta merupakan perguruan tinggi negeri yang berfokus pada pendidikan vokasi. Program pendidikan PNJ mencakup bidang rekayasa dan tata niaga dengan pilihan jenjang Diploma dan Sarjana Terapan. PNJ berlokasi di Kampus Universitas Indonesia, Depok. Pendidikan vokasi di PNJ memadukan pembelajaran teori dan praktik untuk membekali mahasiswa dengan kompetensi yang sesuai dengan kebutuhan dunia kerja. Visi Misi Politeknik Negeri Jakarta Visi Menjadi politeknik unggul bertaraf internasional untuk mendukung daya saing bangsa. Misi Menyelenggarakan Pendidikan Vokasi yang berbasis ilmu pengetahuan, teknologi, rekayasa dan seni yang menghasilkan lulusan berkarakter dan bertakwa kepada Tuhan Yang Maha Esa. Mengembangkan penelitian, peningkatan, dan penerapan ilmu pengetahuan, teknologi, rekayasa dan seni serta produk inovasi berkualitas guna meningkatkan daya saing bangsa. Mengembangkan institusi yang efsien, efektif dan akuntabel berbasis teknologi informasi dan komunikasi Keunggulan Politeknik Negeri Jakarta 1. Fokus pada Pendidikan Vokasi PNJ berfokus pada pendidikan vokasi yang menggabungkan pembelajaran teori dan praktik untuk membekali mahasiswa dengan keterampilan profesional. 2. Pilihan Program Studi Beragam PNJ menyediakan berbagai program studi di bidang teknik, teknologi, bisnis, akuntansi, administrasi, grafika, dan penerbitan. 3. Pilihan Jenjang D3 dan D4 Calon mahasiswa dapat memilih program Diploma III (D3) maupun Sarjana Terapan (D4) sesuai dengan bidang yang diminati. Jurusan dan Program Studi PNJ PNJ memiliki tujuh jurusan utama dengan berbagai pilihan program studi. Jurusan Teknik Sipil Bagi yang tertarik dengan konstruksi dan infrastruktur, PNJ menyediakan beberapa pilihan program studi di bidang teknik sipil. Program Studi: D3 Konstruksi Sipil D3 Konstruksi Gedung D4 Teknik Perancangan Jalan dan Jembatan D4 Teknik Konstruksi Gedung Jurusan Teknik Mesin Program studi di bidang mesin, manufaktur, energi, dan alat berat. Program Studi: D3 Teknik Mesin D3 Teknik Konversi Energi D3 Alat Berat D4 Teknologi Rekayasa Manufaktur D4 Teknologi Rekayasa Pembangkit Energi D4 Teknologi Rekayasa Konversi Energi D4 Teknologi Rekayasa Pemeliharaan Alat Berat Jurusan Teknik Elektro Pilihan program studi di bidang elektronika, kelistrikan, telekomunikasi, dan otomasi. Program Studi: D3 Elektronika Industri D3 Teknik Listrik D3 Telekomunikasi D4 Instrumentasi Kontrol Industri D4 Teknik Otomasi Listrik Industri D4 Broadband Multimedia Jurusan Teknik Informatika dan Komputer Cocok bagi calon mahasiswa yang tertarik dengan informatika, multimedia, jaringan, dan keamanan siber. Program Studi: D4 Teknik Informatika D4 Teknik Multimedia Digital D4 Teknik Multimedia dan Jaringan D4 Rekayasa Keamanan Siber D1 Teknik Komputer dan Jaringan Jurusan Akuntansi Menyediakan program studi di bidang akuntansi, keuangan, dan perbankan. Program Studi: D3 Akuntansi D3 Keuangan dan Perbankan D4 Akuntansi Keuangan D4 Keuangan dan Perbankan D4 Keuangan dan Perbankan Syariah D4 Manajemen Keuangan Jurusan Administrasi Niaga Pilihan program studi di bidang administrasi bisnis, pemasaran, MICE, dan komunikasi bisnis. Program Studi: D3 Administrasi Bisnis D4 Administrasi Bisnis Terapan D4 Usaha Jasa Konvensi, Perjalanan Insentif dan Pameran/MICE D4 Bahasa Inggris untuk Komunikasi Bisnis dan Profesional Jurusan Teknik Grafika dan Penerbitan Menyediakan program studi di bidang penerbitan, grafika, desain, dan teknologi industri cetak. Program Studi: D3 Penerbitan D3 Teknik Grafika D4 Desain Grafis D4 Teknologi Industri Cetak Kemasan D4 Teknologi Rekayasa Cetak dan Grafis 3 Dimensi Pascasarjana PNJ juga menyediakan program pendidikan pascasarjana. Program Studi: S2 Magister Rekayasa Teknologi Manufaktur S2 Magister Teknik Elektro PMB Politeknik Negeri Jakarta 2026 Penerimaan mahasiswa baru PNJ Tahun Akademik 2026/2027 tersedia melalui beberapa jalur, termasuk SNBP, SNBT, Ujian Mandiri, dan Mandiri Prestasi. Selain itu, PNJ juga menyediakan program kerja sama pada jalur penerimaan tertentu. Jalur Masuk PNJ 2026 1. SNBP SNBP merupakan jalur seleksi nasional berdasarkan prestasi akademik dan ketentuan yang berlaku. Calon mahasiswa mengikuti proses seleksi melalui mekanisme SNBP. 2. SNBT SNBT merupakan jalur seleksi nasional berbasis tes. Peserta yang memilih PNJ mengikuti ketentuan seleksi nasional dan proses penetapan biaya pendidikan sesuai ketentuan yang berlaku. 3. Ujian Mandiri Ujian Mandiri (UM) merupakan jalur seleksi PNJ melalui ujian online berbasis kemampuan akademis. Pada 2026, pendaftaran Ujian Mandiri berlangsung pada 1 April–4 Juni 2026. Ujian online dilaksanakan pada 6 Juni 2026, sedangkan pengumuman hasil seleksi dijadwalkan pada 14 Juni 2026. Jalur ini tersedia untuk program reguler dan program kerja sama. 4. Mandiri Prestasi Jalur Mandiri Prestasi ditujukan bagi calon mahasiswa yang memiliki prestasi sesuai ketentuan PNJ. body_text: Company also releases updated investor presentation LOS ANGELES, Calif. — Cadiz, Inc. Its assets include Cadiz Ranch, the largest agricultural operation in San Bernardino County; the Mojave Groundwater Bank, one of the largest new water supply and groundwater storage projects in the Lower Colorado River Basin; and ATEC Water Systems, which provides specialized groundwater treatment technology throughout the western United States. title: Do Moms Really Know Best? Netflix Releases the Trailer for 'Mom Knows Best?,' a New Reality Show Hosted by Claudia Raia
summary: This Thursday, August 13, Netflix released the trailer and announced the contestants for Mom Knows Best?, a new original-format Brazilian reality show hosted by Claudia Raia.
body_text: São Paulo, August 13, 2026 - Moms always know best… or do they? This Thursday, August 13, Netflix released the trailer and announced the contestants for Mom Knows Best? , a new original-format Brazilian reality show hosted by Claudia Raia. The seven-episode season will be released in two parts, with the first four episodes premiering on August 26 , and the final three episodes available on September 2 . (Credit: Nat Odenbreit / Netflix) (Credit: Nat Odenbreit / Netflix) Nine mothers, a prize of up to R$1 million, and the certainty that they know their children better than anyone — they’re at the heart of the game! While the mothers secretly watch their children’s every move, the children believe they’re taking part in a completely different reality show, living together in a student house and facing situations that constantly put their mothers’ predictions about them to the test. To take home the prize, the mothers will have to prove just how well they really know the children they brought into the world. Hosted by Claudia Raia and produced by Boxfish in partnership with Farra, Mom Knows Best? turns the relationship between mothers and their children into a fun and heartwarming competition. With surprising revelations, touching moments, and plenty of laughs, the reality show celebrates one of life’s strongest bonds, inviting viewers to laugh, share the emotion, reflect on their own relationships and, of course, root for these proud moms. Meet the contestants: Adriana Alves (Mom) and Pedro Alves (Son) Ana Martinha Silva (Mom) and Kaynara Silva (Daughter) Carla Luvise (Mom) and Patrick Luvise (Son) Cassia Marques (Mom) and Rafaela Marques (Daughter) Cenir Araujo (Mom) and Karina Araujo (Daughter) Daniela Bernardi (Mom) and Monique Bernardi (Daughter) Dri Varraschim (Mom) and Diego Varraschim (Son) Inocência Cruz (Mom) and Vicktoria Cruz (Daughter) Monica Santos (Mom) and Beatriz Santos (Daughter) Mom Knows Best? premieres August 26, only on Netflix. About Netflix Netflix is one of the world’s leading entertainment services offering TV series, films, games and live programming across a wide variety of genres and languages. Members can play, pause and resume watching as much as they want, anytime, anywhere, and can change their plans at any time. About Boxfish BOXFISH is one of the leading independent production companies currently operating, with offices in Buenos Aires, Madrid, and São Paulo. Founded in 2018 by Diego Guebel, founder of Cuatro Cabezas, the production company behind formats such as CQC, BOXFISH combines experience, creativity, and an international outlook in the development and production of original projects, as well as format adaptations. With a strong presence in entertainment, the company works with some of the market’s leading broadcasters and platforms, including HBO, Netflix, TelevisaUnivision, TV Globo, RecordTV, Amazon Prime, GNT, Telefe, Antena 3, and TVE. Since its launch, BOXFISH has continued to grow and stands out for its ability to develop distinctive projects with broad appeal and strong international potential. About Farra Farra is a Brazilian production company and format creator with a strong presence across streaming, television, branded entertainment, podcasts, film and social media. Founded by executive producer Gui Vieira and writers Gui Cintra and André Brandt — the duo behind original formats such as Mom Knows Best? — the company combines production expertise with the development of innovative content. Over the years, Farra has created, developed, and produced projects for major industry players including Netflix, Globo, HBO, Amazon, and Paramount. Press Kit Agência Ágora | netflix@agora.site

title: Best Shiftnow Alternatives and Competitors
summary: Compare the best ShiftNow alternatives and competitors, including staffing platforms, agencies, and job boards, to find faster fill rates, better worker reliability, and stronger hiring control.
body_text: If you are comparing the best ShiftNow alternatives and competitors, Instawork is a strong option for businesses that need faster fill rates, better worker reliability, and more control over shift staffing. This page compares Instawork with staffing platforms, staffing agencies, and job boards so you can choose the right hiring model for your operation. You can also review this guide to staffing platform alternatives if you want a broader look at on-demand staffing options. Best Shiftnow Alternatives and Competitors Instawork Trustpilot Rating: 4 Instawork is a strong ShiftNow alternative for businesses that need speed and consistency at scale. Businesses can post shifts for seasonal work, temporary work, long-term projects, and full-time hiring. Instawork has a pool of more than 10 million vetted local workers across the U.S. and Canada. The platform fills shifts from two hours to less than 24 hours, with a fill rate above 90%. Worker show rates exceed 98%, and 93% of the time businesses want the same workers back. Businesses also get automated clock-in and clock-out, geofencing, skill vetting support, and a simple app and browser experience. ShiftNow ShiftNow is part of the on-demand staffing category and may work for businesses that want shift-based labor access. Compared with Instawork, businesses should assess local worker depth, fill consistency, and worker return rates before deciding. If repeat usage and fast multi-shift coverage matter, platform scale and vetting quality become more important. Wonolo Trustpilot Rating: 2.4 Wonolo is another on-demand labor platform used for hourly staffing. It can be a fit for warehouse, event, and general labor needs. Compared with ShiftNow, businesses should review how quickly shifts fill in each market and how often workers return for repeat assignments. Instawork stands out when reliability, show rate, and large local supply are key priorities. Bluecrew Bluecrew combines hourly staffing technology with W-2 labor models in some use cases. This can appeal to businesses that want more structure around worker classification. Compared with ShiftNow, it may suit operations with recurring labor demand. Businesses should compare local coverage, lead time, pricing model, and worker quality controls before choosing. Robert Half Trustpilot Rating: 1.8 Robert Half is better known as a staffing agency for office, finance, and professional roles. It can be a practical ShiftNow alternative if your hiring needs are less shift-driven and more role-specific. Compared with staffing platforms, agency models often involve more recruiter support but may move slower for same-day or next-day hourly labor needs. Randstad Trustpilot Rating: 2 Randstad is a large staffing agency with broad category coverage. It may fit businesses that want traditional staffing support across industrial, office, and administrative roles. Compared with ShiftNow, Randstad may be a better fit for planned hiring, while staffing marketplaces can be stronger for rapid shift fill and flexible volume changes. Manpower Manpower is a long-standing staffing company serving many industries. It can work well for businesses that prefer a traditional agency relationship. Compared with ShiftNow, businesses should consider whether they need recruiter-led placement or self-serve shift posting. For urgent labor gaps, platform speed may matter more than agency process. Adecco Trustpilot Rating: 3.2 Adecco offers temporary staffing and workforce solutions across a wide range of roles. It is a reasonable alternative for businesses that want established staffing support. Compared with ShiftNow, Adecco may suit planned staffing programs better than urgent hourly shift coverage. Review speed, markup clarity, and local branch strength before choosing. Indeed Trustpilot Rating: 2 Indeed is a job board rather than a staffing provider. It helps businesses attract applicants, but the employer still handles screening, scheduling, and no-show risk. Compared with ShiftNow, Indeed can offer broader reach for direct hiring, but it is usually less useful when you need vetted workers ready for shifts on short notice. ZipRecruiter Trustpilot Rating: 4.5 ZipRecruiter is another job board and hiring platform that supports applicant sourcing. It may fit businesses building a direct hiring funnel. Compared with ShiftNow, it offers less staffing support after a job post goes live. If speed to coverage is the main goal, a labor marketplace may reduce manual hiring work. LinkedIn Trustpilot Rating: 1.2 LinkedIn is often used for professional recruiting and employer branding. It can be useful for full-time hiring and specialized roles. Compared with ShiftNow, it is not built for fast hourly shift fill. Businesses that need immediate staffing coverage should weigh direct sourcing tools against platforms designed for rapid labor dispatch. How To Choose The Right Staffing Alternative Can The Platform Fill Shifts Quickly? Speed matters when callouts disrupt operations. Compare how fast each option can deliver confirmed workers. Staffing platforms usually move faster than agencies or job boards for urgent coverage. Are The Workers Reliable And Vetted? Reliability affects service quality, overtime costs, and manager workload. Look for vetting, worker ratings, show rate visibility, and repeat worker usage. Strong worker quality controls reduce shift risk. Do You Need Flexible Hiring Models? Some businesses need one system for temporary shifts, long-term temporary work, and full-time hiring. Choosing a provider that supports all three can lower admin time and simplify workforce planning. Why Businesses Look For Shiftnow Alternatives Businesses usually look for ShiftNow alternatives when they need more worker supply, better fill consistency, stronger vetting, or faster support for urgent demand. Some also want clearer pricing, better time tracking, and tools that help bring back top workers. Others need a solution that supports both short-term shifts and longer hiring plans in one platform. Choose Instawork If You Need Speed and Reliability Can Instawork Fill Shifts Fast? Instawork fills shifts from two hours to less than 24 hours. Its fill rate is above 90%, compared with an industry average of 50% to 60%. Are Instawork Workers Reliable And Vetted? Instawork has more than 10 million vetted local workers in the U.S. and Canada. Worker show rates exceed 98%, and businesses rate workers after each shift with an average rating of 4.8 out of 5. Do You Get More Workforce Control? Businesses can post shifts, rate workers, and bring back strong performers. Ninety-three percent of the time, businesses want the same workers to return. Automated clock-in and clock-out with geofencing also improve billing accuracy and arrival tracking. Is Pricing More Transparent? Instawork gives businesses a simple platform experience through app and browser access. Businesses can manage staffing in one place and reduce manual coordination common with agencies and job boards.

title: 10 Quick Ways to Make 500 Dollars Fast in 2026
summary: Need cash now? Discover 10 legitimate and quick ways to make 500 dollars. Explore gig work, freelancing, and more actionable tips for fast earnings.
body_text: Join Gerald for a new way to manage your finances. Cash advances with no fees. Get Started Need $500 fast? You're probably not trying to build a side business right now. You're trying to cover a rent shortfall, fix a car, replace a broken appliance, or stop one overdue bill from turning into three. The fastest quick ways to make 500 dollars usually come from the same place, short bursts of labor, selling things you already own, or combining a few methods so the money lands sooner. That's why this list is organized around speed and access, not theory. Some options can start paying within days, some need a weekend of hustle, and a few work best when you already have cash flow pressure and need to bridge the gap before payday. A tool like Gerald can matter here because it helps with timing, using interest-free cash advances , BNPL for essentials , and mobile service options to keep necessities covered while you chase the money. If you're living paycheck to paycheck, the game isn't perfection. It's picking the fastest option you can start today, then stacking the next one if the first doesn't get you all the way to $500. Table of Contents 1. Gig Economy Work How to make it work faster 2. Freelance Services What usually sells fastest 3. Online Reselling Items that usually sell faster 4. Tutoring and Teaching Services What helps tutoring get booked 5. Selling Digital Products What helps digital products move 6. Selling Photos Online What usually improves your odds 7. Cashback and Rewards Programs Where this helps most 8. Micro Tasks and Online Job Platforms How to avoid the trap 9. Plasma and Blood Donation Centers What to expect before you go 10. Selling Used Items What helps used items move faster 10 Quick Ways to Make $500, Comparison Your Next Step to Earning $500 1. Gig Economy Work Gig work stays one of the fastest ways to pull in cash because the jobs are short, repeatable, and easy to stack. Delivery driving, rideshare, virtual assistance, house cleaning, and pet care all fit that pattern, and one finance guide says delivery-based work can take about 20 to 25 hours at around $20 to $25 per hour to reach the goal, which is why this category keeps showing up for people who need money in a week or less Moneylion . For someone living between irregular paychecks, the appeal is straightforward. You can work around a day job, take the busiest shifts, and stop once you hit the target. That flexibility also fits people using Gerald's work and income resources to handle weeks when income does not line up with bills. How to make it work faster Practical rule: Don't chase every app at once. Pick two platforms, learn the busiest hours, and stay consistent long enough to get the better offers. Focus on peak demand: Lunch, dinner, and weekends usually give you the best shot at faster earnings because customers and clients are already active. Keep your costs visible: Fuel, mileage, and car wear can cut into take-home cash, so track them from the start instead of guessing later. Protect your rating: Better ratings usually lead to better jobs, especially on task platforms where customers compare workers quickly. Use cash-flow tools wisely: If a repair or refill would stop you from working, a short-term advance can keep you earning instead of forcing you off the road. The main trade-off is clear, you give up time and put wear on your body or car in exchange for speed. That works if your goal is to get to $500 quickly, but it is a poor fit if you are already stretched thin and cannot absorb upfront costs like gas, tires, childcare, or slow payouts. 2. Freelance Services Freelancing works because you are selling a skill, not just hours. Writing, design, virtual assistance, and coding can move quickly if you already know what you offer and can explain it in plain language, especially on platforms like Fiverr, Upwork, 99designs, and Freelancer where buyers are already searching for help. The fastest wins usually come from services a buyer can grasp in one sentence, like a landing page rewrite, a logo refresh, inbox cleanup, or spreadsheet help. The strongest edge here is repeatability. Once you finish one assignment well, you can reuse that sample to help land the next one. That matters when cash is tight, because even a small buffer can cover the friction that keeps freelancers stuck, like software, internet access, printing, or getting to a client meeting. A smart freelancer usually starts with one narrow offer instead of five. If you write, do not pitch “all writing.” Pitch blog posts for local service businesses, because the buyer can understand the need and say yes faster. If you design, show three polished samples instead of a huge portfolio full of mixed work. A clear offer reduces back-and-forth, and that often matters more than having a long list of skills. What usually sells fastest Technical writing and content writing: Clear, useful deliverables are easier to sell than vague “creative services.” Virtual assistance: Admin work, inbox organization, scheduling, and research are easy for clients to outsource quickly. Social media support: Businesses often need help posting, captioning, or cleaning up their content calendars. Simple design jobs: Logos, flyers, and branded graphics can close faster than larger custom projects. A practical way to start is to pick one service, one type of buyer, and one sample you can show immediately. That keeps your pitch focused and makes it easier for a client to picture the result. If you already have a few past projects, package them as proof of speed and reliability instead of trying to sell every skill at once. This category can bring in quick cash, but it is not instant unless you already have a profile, samples, or a network. The first sale may take effort and a few slow replies. After that, it can become one of the cleaner ways to build toward $500 without needing inventory or a vehicle. 3. Online Reselling Reselling works fast because you can turn items you already own, or can source cheaply, into cash without waiting on a long client process. If you need money quickly, start with the stuff already sitting in your home before you spend time hunting for inventory. A practical reselling guide also points out that many households have several hundred dollars in unused items that can be sold, and a focused weekend of listing can bring in meaningful cash WalletGrower . That makes closets, garages, and spare rooms the first place to check. There are two ways to do it. One is flipping, where you buy low and resell higher. The other is clearing out your own belongings, which usually moves faster because you do not have to source anything first. If the goal is to cover a bill or bridge a cash gap this week, your own items are the cleaner starting point. A little extra cash flow can make this easier to pull off. If you are waiting for a sale to clear or need a small cushion to buy a few higher-confidence items, Gerald's retail support resources can help reduce the pressure while the listings are moving. Items that usually sell faster Vintage clothing and branded apparel: These are easy to photograph, compare against sold listings, and ship without much hassle. Electronics: Phones, game consoles, tablets, and laptop accessories tend to attract buyers when they are tested and described clearly. Collectibles and books: Items with a built-in audience can move without a long negotiation cycle. Furniture or bundles: Larger pieces can produce one bigger payout instead of several small sales. Good listings matter more than people expect. Clear photos, exact condition notes, and the right brand names cut down on questions and help buyers decide faster. The main mistake is buying random inventory without checking what sells in your area or online. Reselling only feels automatic from the outside. Fast sales usually come from items you can move quickly, not from guessing on whatever looks trendy. 4. Tutoring and Teaching Services Tutoring is one of the fastest ways to bring in money if you already know a subject well enough to explain it clearly. Math, science, standardized test prep, language support, and music lessons are the easiest places to start because parents and students already understand why they pay for help. You are not trying to sell the idea of tutoring itself, you are showing that you can solve one specific problem. A single student can be worth a lot more than a one-off task. Tutoring usually gets booked in sessions or packages, which makes it easier to reach $500 without building a huge client base. That matters if you are living paycheck-to-paycheck and need cash flow now, because a few committed students can add up faster than a long list of small errands. High-stakes exams and hard school subjects tend to create the strongest urgency. If you already have a credential, use it. A degree, certification, test score, or teaching background makes the offer easier to trust, especially when a parent is deciding quickly. What helps tutoring get booked Local visibility matters: Community boards, parent groups, and a simple business profile can bring in nearby students without platform fees. Packages close faster than single sessions: Parents are often more willing to commit when they can book several sessions upfront. Test prep is usually easier to price: SAT, ACT, and similar services feel outcome-driven, which makes the pitch clearer. Show your subject and level clearly: A student or parent should know within seconds what you teach and who it is for. If online tutoring feels slow at first, in-person sessions can sometimes book faster because the trust factor comes from convenience and location. A student can meet at a library, coffee shop, or home office, and you avoid the waiting period that sometimes comes with marketplace apps. There is a trade-off, though. You need to prepare before every session, because tutoring falls apart quickly when it feels disorganized. If you know the subject, can explain it calmly, and keep the session structured, this can be one of the better quick-income options that also builds a steadier weekly side income later. 5. Selling Digital Products Digital products are not the fastest way to get cash if you are starting from zero today, but they can still fit a short-term money plan when you want limited ongoing work after the first sale. Templates, eBooks, presets, and mini-courses are appealing because you make them once and keep reselling them. The practical upside is straightforward, once the product is built, you are not swapping another hour of work for every purchase. A challenge lies in ensuring the product addresses a problem people already recognize. A clever idea is usually weaker than a validated niche. Canva templates, Notion templates, resume templates, and similar products tend to outperform vague “general productivity” offers because the buyer can understand the use case right away. A simple scenario helps here. Someone short on cash may not have time to build a large catalog, so the better move is to create one narrow product that solves one obvious problem and get it listed fast. What helps digital products move Build a minimum viable version first: A useful product beats a perfect product that never ships. Write for search: Etsy, Gumroad, and your own site all depend on discoverability. Bundle strategically: A template plus a short guide usually sells better than a lone file. Promote where the audience already spends time: Email, Instagram, Pinterest, TikTok, and YouTube each play a different role, but the product still has to solve a narrow problem. Speed matters here, but so does cash flow. If you are living paycheck to paycheck, a platform like Gerald can help cover a small gap while you create and list the product, which makes the slower setup period easier to handle without derailing your budget. The trade-off is timing. If you need money tonight, this is not the fastest route. If you can spend a day or two making something useful, it can become one of the cleaner ways to stop relying only on labor for every dollar. 6. Selling Photos Online Selling photos online works best as a slow-burn income stream, and that fits this article because it turns images you already shot into repeatable use. If your camera roll already has usable photos, or you can work through shoots quickly, microstock platforms can generate long-tail sales from content that would otherwise just sit on your phone or hard drive. For someone trying to stretch every dollar, that matters. It gives you a way to build an asset library instead of relying only on one-off labor. Practical images are easier for designers and marketers to slot into real projects, which is why they are more likely to get licensed again. A useful approach is to shoot with a buyer's needs in mind, not just your own portfolio goals. This usually will not fix a same-day cash crunch unless you already have a portfolio and some sales history. It works better as a side stream for people who can keep building while they handle immediate bills through other methods. If money is tight right now, a platform like Gerald can help cover a short gap while you upload, keyword, and organize your photos, which makes the slower setup period easier to manage without throwing off your budget. For that reason, stock photos belong in the asset-building bucket, not the emergency bucket. 7.
